title: Stream preview hot paths and remove extraction hash overhead
description: Bounded performance slice under TSK-0008 / TSK-0065. Current user-supplied editor logs show steady-state generation dominated by FieldSampling (~387-408 ms) and AppearanceBake (~189-196 ms), with optimized MeshExtraction usually ~113-117 ms and occasional contour-resolution variance. Implemented three behavior-preserving reductions: row-oriented Burst SDF sampling removes per-sample flat-index division/modulo and reduces scratch to per-work-item row batches; streamed Burst appearance resolution removes the vertexCount × programCount distance matrix while preserving absolute-distance and Body tie semantics; direct integer grid corner/edge ownership replaces the extraction Dictionary<long,int> with deterministic dense ownership tables and overflow guards. Acceptance requires Unity parity/determinism/topology validation and fresh benchmark measurements before marking complete.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Implementation round 2026-09-10: DensityGrid.SamplePortable now uses row-oriented Burst sampling with bounded per-work-item scratch isolation and contiguous x traversal. AppearanceBaker routes nearest appearance selection through the consolidated AppearanceResolveBurst streamed candidate reducer instead of a full distance matrix and merge pass. MarchingCubesExtractor now uses GridVertexOwnership with direct integer corner/X-edge/Y-edge/Z-edge slots and owner+1 sentinel encoding. Existing AppearanceBakerTests already contain Bake_BurstResolve_MatchesManagedResolveExactly; existing extraction tests cover watertightness and welding invariants. Unity test execution and fresh benchmark comparison remain pending in this environment.

comments.author: user
comments.body: User-supplied Quality 16 steady-state editor logs: TotalGeneration 701.9, 700.6, 798.8, 720.5, 702.8 ms; FieldSampling 386.8-407.5 ms; MeshExtraction 112.6-208.9 ms, normally ~113-117 ms except one 208.9 ms run driven by MeshContourResolution 147 ms; MeshValidation ~5 ms; AppearanceBake 188.7-196.0 ms. Mesh output was stable at 20,962 triangles / 10,483 vertices. These measurements are the post-threading-fix baseline supplied by the user and should be compared with the new implementation after Unity warm-up.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Review correction before validation: the first row-batching implementation shared one scratch buffer across parallel work items, which could race. The current implementation allocates bounded per-work-item scratch slices (RowsPerExecute chosen under an 8 MB budget) and offsets each row into its own slice. The unsafe version is no longer the branch state.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Second static council re-audit 2026-09-11: no regression was found in the corrected row-batched sampler, streamed appearance reducer, or dense extraction ownership. One additional resource-lifetime defect was found outside the prior slice: the public AppearanceBaker.Bake cleanup scope did not cover a failure during body-program compilation, so compiled part programs could leak on that exception path. Fixed in 13c72f2fcaa3704319aa45dd8b581ba810eefef8. Follow-up performance/design findings are tracked under TSK-0201 through TSK-0203; Unity compilation, parity, topology, determinism, and fresh benchmarks remain mandatory gates.

comments.author: ChatGPT
comments.body: Critical correction 2026-09-11: the pushed row-batched sampler was still incorrect. SdfSamplingRowBatchJob.Execute calculated rowValueOffset from localRow only, so all parallel work items reused scratch offsets 0..RowsPerExecute-1 and raced each other. This matches the user's nondeterministic detached polygons and the failing GenerationIntegrity/FastFieldSampling tests. The production sampler is now fixed to add a disjoint workItemScratchOffset per work item, with checked index arithmetic. Unity rerun is required to close this task.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: Post-pull reconciliation (2026-09-11). Pulled commit `656243f` claims to fix the sampler scratch race but only added the `workItemIndex` offset; `DensityGrid.cs:89` still allocates `ScratchValues` for one work-item batch (`rowScratchLength * rowsPerExecute`), so the new per-work-item offsets run past the buffer for `workItemIndex >= 1`. The pulled audit `docs/audits/creaturecreator-sdf-sampling-race-fix-audit-26-09-11-21-50-00.md` records the race as repaired and asserts the allocation "already reserves enough storage" — that assertion is refuted by source. This task's Unity validation gate must include: scratch allocation sized for the concurrent work-item set (proven by offset/bounds derivation, not one run), the direct parallel regression passing with a correctly sized scratch buffer, and repeated fingerprint determinism. Incomplete-fix scope is tracked as `TSK-0212`.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body:
Sampler scratch fix validated end-to-end (2026-09-11). `DensityGrid.SamplePortable` now bounds the scheduled work-item set to `ScratchValueBudget` and processes rows in windows; `SdfSamplingRowBatchJob` takes `RowStart`. This removes the silent out-of-bounds scratch writes that the pushed work-item offset introduced.

Evidence:
- EditMode 148/148 passed. PlayMode full 751 total / 709 passed / 42 failed (`TestResults.xml`, complete list recovered by recursive parse past the runner's 25-cap).
- The determinism cluster recorded in `TSK-0194` now passes: `FastFieldSamplingTests.FastCulling_IsDeterministic`, `GenerationIntegrityTests.SampleAndExtract_RepeatedRuns_AreBitIdentical`, `CanonicalMorphologyChainTests` x3, `GeneratedCreatureTests` x3, `CreatureGenerationSchedulerTests.AsyncGeneration_MatchesSynchronousMeshAndColors`. 12 recorded failures resolved in total.
- Editor: 4 regenerations on unchanged DNA/settings gave 20962 triangles / 10483 vertices every time; TotalGeneration 1314.8 ms (cold), 789.0, 779.9, 707.4 ms — inside the documented 701.9–798.8 ms baseline. No detached islands.
- Screenshot: `Assets/Screenshots/cc-sdf-race-fix-scene-2026-09-11.png`.

Remaining 42 PlayMode failures are pre-existing non-sampler clusters (skeleton/bone, marching-cubes winding, influence domains, non-finite validation, FABRIK/IK). See `TSK-0212` for the acceptance-criteria disposition and `TSK-0194` for the full delta.

Note: an earlier copy of this comment was mis-routed to `tsk-0198-define-portable-animation-clip-and-sampling-contract` because the bare key `TSK-0198` is colliding between two records (see `TSK-0213`). This record is the perf/extraction owner and is the intended target.
